q: A river 216 m wide flows at 10 m/s. A boat with speed 10 m/s in still water is steered at 53° to the perpendicular, tilted upstream. How far downstream of the point directly opposite does it land? (Take sin 37° = 0.6, cos 37° = 0.8.)
s:
Across the river: v⊥ = 10 cos 53° = 6 m/s, so t = 216 ÷ 6 = 36 s.
Along the bank: 10 − 10 sin 53° = 10 − 8 = 2 m/s (downstream).
Drift = 2 × 36 = 72 m

q:
A thief runs at 6 m/s along a straight road. A policeman 55 m behind him starts chasing at 11 m/s. How long does he take to catch the thief?
Give the answer in s.
s:
Both move in the same direction, so the gap closes at the difference of the speeds.
Closing speed = 11 − 6 = 5 m/s.
t = 55 ÷ 5
= 11 s

q:
A river 44 m wide flows at 6 m/s. A boat with speed 5 m/s in still water is steered at 37° to the perpendicular, tilted upstream. How far downstream of the point directly opposite does it land? (Take sin 37° = 0.6, cos 37° = 0.8.)
Give the answer in m.
s:
Across the river: v⊥ = 5 cos 37° = 4 m/s, so t = 44 ÷ 4 = 11 s.
Along the bank: 6 − 5 sin 37° = 6 − 3 = 3 m/s (downstream).
Drift = 3 × 11 = 33 m

q: A motor boat goes 160 m downstream and then returns 160 m upstream. Its speed in still water is 10 m/s and the river flows at 6 m/s. Find the total time for the round trip.
s:
Downstream speed = 10 + 6 = 16 m/s, so t₁ = 160 ÷ 16 = 10 s.
Upstream speed = 10 − 6 = 4 m/s, so t₂ = 160 ÷ 4 = 40 s.
Total = 10 + 40 = 50 s

q: An aeroplane is headed due east with an air speed of 32 km h⁻¹ while a wind blows due north at 24 km h⁻¹. How far does the aeroplane move relative to the ground in 4 h?
s:
Velocity over the ground = velocity in air + wind velocity (vectors).
The two are perpendicular: v = √(32² + 24²) = 40 km h⁻¹.
Distance = 40 × 4
= 160 km

q: A cyclist riding at 9 m/s on level ground finds that the rain, which actually falls vertically, appears to come at 37° to the vertical. Find the actual speed of the rain. (Take tan 37° = 3/4.)
s:
Seen from the cyclist, the rain has a horizontal component equal to his speed and a vertical component equal to the rain speed.
tan 37° = {9;v(rain)} = 3/4
v(rain) = 9 ÷ (3/4) = 12 m/s

s:
The trains close the gap at 7 + 8 = 15 m/s, so they meet after t = 570 ÷ 15 = 38 s.
The bird flies the whole time, at constant speed.
Distance = 32 × 38
= 1216 m

q: Rain falls vertically at 40 km h⁻¹. A man cycles on level ground at 30 km h⁻¹. Find the speed of the rain relative to the cyclist.
